guide.coordinates: All x/y values are pixels from the atlas top-left. X increases right and Y down. Rectangles use x,y,w,h with exclusive right/bottom. Indices are zero-based; source_row and column are one-based. Global frame_size is the legacy 64px actor default only. This atlas has mixed frame sizes: always read each frame rect.w/rect.h. Wisp frames are native 32x32.
guide.anchors: anchor is relative to the untrimmed 64x64 frame. The fixed rendering pivot (32,32) matches src/assets/sprites.ts actor px/py. anchor_in_atlas is a locator, not a second offset. Anchor is not measured from feet or visible bounds; never recenter crouches, leaps, falls or empty death frames. Wisp overrides the actor default with (16,16), from its approved source metadata. Read each frame's anchor; do not force Wisp to (32,32).
guide.draw_formula: For screen anchor (dx,dy) and scale s: drawImage(atlas, rect.x,rect.y,rect.w,rect.h, dx-anchor.x*s,dy-anchor.y*s,rect.w*s,rect.h*s). Native scale s=1 preserves 32px Wisp beside 64px actors.
guide.visible_bounds: Optional tight alpha bounds within the frame, for inspection only. Null means fully transparent (intentional on some death endings). Frames are not trimmed or rotated.
guide.flame_center_anchor: Where present, the RGB-key flame pixel centroid in frame-local coordinates, useful as a VFX/light attachment point. It is not the torch grip, mesh tip or rendering pivot.
guide.directions: Each animation block contains eight rows: north,northeast,east,southeast,south,southwest,west,northwest. Columns play left to right. Atlas block placement is arbitrary: always use listed frame rects. Wisp is an explicit exception: its three rows are center, left, right eye-look variants, not eight compass headings. Use wisp/fire_loop.directions[look][frame].rect, selecting one look at a time.
guide.timing: gameplay durations use explicit frame_durations_ms first, then gameplay_frame_duration_ms, otherwise 1000/fps. Preview-only holds remain separate and must not silently replace gameplay timing. Original metadata is embedded for end states and action-specific decisions.
guide.loop: Use animation.loop and source metadata for one-shot endings. If source omitted loop, only idle/walk/run were inferred to loop, with loop_inferred_from_action_name=true.
guide.palette_swap: For lit PLAYER frame rectangles only, start from the unchanged base pixels; replace exact base outer/middle/core RGB with the selected copper/sodium/strontium roles. Preserve all alpha and all other RGB. Apply to frame regions only, never labels, palettes or enemy frames. Several palettes may share RGB values; they are not global atlas-wide remaps. Wisp has its own six-colour body palette. Do not treat it as a lit player torch or remap its colours to the shared enemy palette.
guide.sampling: Nearest/point filtering, no mipmaps or linear interpolation. Source animation pixels are copied exactly with transparent native margins. Headers and palette panel are opaque reference regions outside frame rects.
guide.integration: Asset-only revision. Use this matching PNG/JSON pair when integrating. Game runtime imports were not modified by this asset export.
guide.references: All finished main sheets are included once; compact sheets and inspection/showcase PNGs are excluded because they duplicate main-frame content. Palette swatches are included here at the user request; existing individual sheets and separate palette files remain unchanged. The approved Wisp source is spritesheets/wisp/wisp.png (36 frames); its equivalent center/left/right strips are not duplicated again.
guide.revision: V2 replaces player walk and both run variants with the approved 8-frame gait. Atlas blocks were repacked, so use this PNG with its matching v2 JSON; v1 coordinates are not interchangeable.
